examples.question_text:
Equipment costs $\$40\,000$. Straight-line depreciation removes $\$4500$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $15\%$ p.a.
Which method gives the lower salvage value after $3$ years? Calculate the total depreciation under each method. Give money answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Straight-line:
$\begin{aligned}S &= V_0-Dn\\ &=40\,000-4500(3)\\ &=\$26\,500.00\end{aligned}$
Declining balance:
$\begin{aligned}S &=V_0(1-r)^n\\ &=40\,000(0.85)^3\\ &=\$24\,565.00\end{aligned}$
Declining balance gives the lower salvage value.
Straight-line total depreciation:
$\begin{aligned}40\,000-26\,500&=\$13\,500.00\end{aligned}$
Declining-balance total depreciation:
$\begin{aligned}40\,000-24\,565&=\$15\,435.00\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A computer costs $\$4800$.
a. Find the annual straight-line depreciation needed for its value to reach zero after $4$ years.
b. Explain, with suitable calculations, why declining-balance depreciation at $25\%$ p.a. never gives a value of zero.
examples.solution_text:
a.
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0-Dn\\0&=4800-4D\\4D&=4800\\D&=\$1200\end{aligned}$
The annual depreciation is $\$1200$.
b.
$S=4800(0.75)^n$
After $4$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S&=4800(0.75)^4\\&=\$1518.75\end{aligned}$
For every finite number of years $n\geq0$, $(0.75)^n>0$, so the value remains positive. Each year removes a percentage of the remaining value.

a. Both graphs start at $\$12\,000$. At $2$ years, the straight-line value is $\$8000$ and the declining-balance value is approximately $\$6750$.
b. The straight line falls from $\$12\,000$ to zero over $6$ years.
$\begin{aligned}D&=\frac{12\,000}{6}\\&=\$2000\end{aligned}$
The annual straight-line depreciation is $\$2000$.
c. At $4$ years the straight line is above the declining-balance curve; at $5$ years it is below. Their intersection after purchase lies between $4$ and $5$ years.

examples.question_text:
An asset costs $\$20\,000$. Straight-line depreciation removes $\$3000$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $25\%$ p.a.
Calculate both salvage values at the end of years $4$ and $5$. Between which two whole years after purchase do the methods give the same value? Give money answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
At $4$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S_{\mathrm{SL}}&=20\,000-3000(4)\\&=\$8000.00\\S_{\mathrm{DB}}&=20\,000(0.75)^4\\&=\$6328.13\end{aligned}$
At $5$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S_{\mathrm{SL}}&=20\,000-3000(5)\\&=\$5000.00\\S_{\mathrm{DB}}&=20\,000(0.75)^5\\&=\$4746.09\end{aligned}$
The straight-line value is still higher at $5$ years, so check year $6$:
$\begin{aligned}S_{\mathrm{SL}}&=20\,000-3000(6)\\&=\$2000.00\\S_{\mathrm{DB}}&=20\,000(0.75)^6\\&=\$3559.57\end{aligned}$
The straight-line value changes from higher to lower between $5$ and $6$ years. The methods give the same value between those years.

examples.question_text:
A vehicle costs $\$45\,000$. It depreciates by $\$3000$ per year using the straight-line method for the first $3$ years. It then depreciates at $20\%$ p.a. using the declining-balance method.
Find its value and total depreciation at the end of $7$ years. Give money answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
First $3$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S&=45\,000-3000(3)\\&=\$36\,000.00\end{aligned}$
Use the changeover value as the starting value for the remaining $7-3=4$ years.
$\begin{aligned}S&=36\,000(0.8)^4\\&=\$14\,745.60\end{aligned}$
Total depreciation:
$\begin{aligned}45\,000-14\,745.60&=\$30\,254.40\end{aligned}$
